title: Installation requires R >= 4.5.0
description: While the package may only need R >= 4.2.0, the instll calls tools::sha256sum(), which is only in R >= 4.5.0

title: r: data references fail for dotted R object names
description:
`r:` data references currently break when the referenced R object name contains a dot, even though dotted names are valid and common in R.

### Reproducible example

Create an `.Rmd` with:

````
---
output: html_document
---

```{r}
library(ggsql)
my.data <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 4:6)
```

```{ggsql}
SELECT * FROM r:my.data
```
````

Then render the document.

### Expected

The chunk should return the table from `my.data`, the same way `r:test_df` works for object names without dots.

### Actual

The chunk fails because the internal DuckDB table name is derived from the raw object name, so `r:my.data` becomes `__r_my.data__`. DuckDB interprets the `.` as a schema separator rather than part of the table name. In local reproduction, that ultimately surfaced as:

```
resolved query: SELECT * FROM __r_my.data__
...
Catalog Error: Table with name data__ does not exist!
...
ERROR: User function panicked: execute_sql_ipc
```

### Why this matters

Dotted names are very common in R, so this makes `r:` references less reliable than they appear. The failure mode is also severe because it can panic instead of producing a normal user-facing error.

A likely fix would be to sanitize the internal registered table names before substituting them into SQL, with collision handling for names like `my.data` and `my_data`.
